title: California Small Claims Court — Filing a Claim
description: Step-by-step guide for filing and winning a small claims case in California. Covers claims up to $12,500 for individuals ($6,250 for businesses).

steps.title: Determine if small claims court is right for your case
steps.description: Small claims court handles money disputes only. You cannot sue for injunctions or to force someone to do something — only for money damages.
actions: Confirm your claim is for money only (not injunctions or specific performance)
Check the claim limit: $12,500 for individuals, $6,250 for businesses, $2,500 for guarantors
Verify you are within the statute of limitations: 2 years for written contracts, 4 years for oral contracts, 3 years for property damage
Confirm you cannot sue in small claims more than twice per calendar year
Identify all defendants (people or businesses you are suing)

deadlines.notes: Missing the statute of limitations permanently bars your claim.

steps.title: Send a demand letter
steps.description: Before filing, send a written demand letter to the defendant. This is required by law for some claims and strengthens your case for all claims.
actions: Write a clear demand letter stating: what happened, amount owed, and a deadline to respond (typically 10-14 days)
Send by certified mail with return receipt requested
Keep a copy and the delivery confirmation
If the defendant is a business, look up their registered agent for service of process

deadlines.notes: Give defendant at least 10 days to respond before filing. This shows good faith.

steps.title: File your claim with the court
steps.description: File Form SC-100 at the Small Claims Division of the Superior Court in the correct county.
actions: Determine the correct court: where the defendant lives or does business, or where the contract was signed/performed
Complete Form SC-100 (Plaintiff's Claim and ORDER to Go to Small Claims Court)
List all defendants with their correct legal names and addresses
State your claim clearly and the exact dollar amount
Pay the filing fee ($30–$75 depending on claim amount) or file Form FW-001 for fee waiver
Receive your court date from the clerk — usually 30-75 days from filing

deadlines.notes: Hearing is typically scheduled 30-75 days after filing.

steps.title: Serve the defendant
steps.description: The defendant must be properly served with the court papers before the hearing. Improper service will result in your case being dismissed.
actions: You CANNOT serve the papers yourself — use a process server, sheriff, or someone 18+ not involved in the case
Serve at least 15 days before the hearing if defendant is in California
Serve at least 20 days before if defendant is outside California
Complete Form SC-104 (Proof of Service) after service
File the Proof of Service with the court BEFORE the hearing
If you cannot serve the defendant, ask the clerk about substitute service options

deadlines.notes: Must serve defendant at least 15 days before hearing (20 if outside CA). File proof of service before hearing date.

steps.agency: Sheriff's Office or Private Process Server

steps.title: Prepare for your hearing
steps.description: Small claims hearings are informal but you must be organised and ready to present your case in 15-20 minutes.
actions: Organise your evidence: contracts, receipts, invoices, photographs, text messages, emails
Prepare a simple written timeline of events
Bring 3 copies of all documents: one for judge, one for defendant, one for yourself
Identify and bring any witnesses who saw what happened
Practice a 2-minute summary of your claim
Calculate your damages precisely and bring itemised list

deadlines.notes: Arrive 30 minutes early. If you miss your hearing without notifying the court, your case will be dismissed.

steps.title: Attend the hearing and receive judgment
steps.description: Present your case to the judge. Judges often mail their decision rather than announcing it in court.
actions: Arrive early and check in with the clerk
When called, briefly explain your case and present evidence
Let the judge guide the process — answer questions directly and honestly
If defendant does not appear, request a default judgment
Judgment may be mailed to you within a few days if not announced at hearing
If you lose, you may appeal to Superior Court within 30 days

deadlines.notes: Appeal must be filed within 30 days of the clerk's mailing of the Notice of Entry of Judgment.

steps.title: Collect your judgment
steps.description: Winning a judgment does not mean automatic payment. You may need to take further steps to collect.
actions: Wait 30 days after judgment for defendant to pay voluntarily or appeal
If unpaid after 30 days, file an Abstract of Judgment (EJ-001) to create a lien on property
Request a Writ of Execution (EJ-130) to have the sheriff garnish wages or bank accounts
Use Form SC-134 to find out where defendant works or banks (debtor's examination)
Judgments are valid for 10 years and can be renewed

deadlines.notes: Defendant has 30 days to pay or appeal. After 30 days you can begin collection.
